title: Derived slice comparison for the finite quotient layer
statement: For an adic coefficient datum with compatible finite coefficient isomorphisms, a residue chart complex P that is bounded above and termwise projective, and the supplied residue chart isomorphism e, the derived restriction to the etale chart of the actual finite quotient layer is isomorphic to the derived restriction of the coefficient-changed constant realization of the explicit ideal-layer tensor complex.

source.place: Tags 094I and 06YU, derived tensor balancing before homology

proof.text: Identify the actual coefficient kernel as the restriction of the constant residue ideal layer, using the ordinary kernel comparison. This retains the successor coefficient action.

Resolve the successor reduction by a K-flat complex. Change of rings preserves K-flatness, and ordinary tensor cancellation gives a natural chain isomorphism. The published degree-zero K-flat tensor comparison and scalar-extension computation give the derived balancing isomorphism. Composition of derived scalar extension and the projection equation identify its residue input with the zeroth reduction of M.

Exact slice restriction preserves K-flat complexes. Its ordinary tensor comparison and the degree-zero tensor calculation give compatibility with tensor by the restricted residue layer. Scalar restriction commutes with slice restriction as an exact functor, hence also on derived categories.

The bounded above projective complex P has a K-flat constant realization: lifting and ring-equivalence restriction preserve projectivity, projective modules are flat, constant realization preserves flatness, and bounded above flat complexes are K-flat. Compute tensor with the layer term by term. The ordinary tensor comparison identifies this complex with the successor constant layer-tensor model. The coefficient isomorphisms make ordinary scalar change exact and identify it with derived scalar change.

Convert the supplied representative-based chart isomorphism to exact derived restriction. Apply the slice tensor and scalar-restriction functors to it, and compose with balancing, slice compatibility, and the explicit chart computation. This proves the original derived slice isomorphism without any change of statement.

proof_origin.place: Tag 094I displayed layer-balancing identity, with Tags 06YU and 06YY; G1 Lean proof from two ordinary comparisons

theorem finiteQuotient_layer_tensor_derived_slice_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t})
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    [∀ n : ℕ, (koszulConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, adicConstantRing X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) ⟶
      completedAdicFiniteCommRing X d n)
    (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (φ n))
    (hcompat : FinitePerfectModelsCompatible X d φ)
    (M : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules X d))
    (b : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (Z : X.Etale)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (0 + 1))) ℤ)
    (hPb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (0 + 1)) (P.X i))
    (e : Nonempty
      (ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d 0)
          ((toProEt X).obj Z) ((completedAdicQuotientReduction X d 0).obj M) ≅
        ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses (completedAdicFiniteRing X d 0)
          ((toProEt X).obj Z) ((completedAdicDerivedChange X (φ 0)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (finiteModelConstantComplex X _ P))))) :
    Nonempty
      ((ringedDerivedRestrictionGeneral (completedAdicFiniteRing X d (n + 1))
          ((toProEt X).obj Z)).obj (finiteQuotientLayerObject X d M n) ≅
        (ringedDerivedRestrictionGeneral (completedAdicFiniteRing X d (n + 1))
          ((toProEt X).obj Z)).obj
          ((completedAdicDerivedChange X (φ (n + 1))).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              (finiteModelConstantComplex X _
                (finiteQuotientLayerTensorComplex d.ideal n P)))))
